summary.text: 武 means “military” or “martial.” One historical explanation combines a weapon, 戈, with a foot or movement sign, 止, suggesting an army on the march. The famous reading “stop the weapons” gives the character an ethical message, but Wiktionary treats that as a reinterpretation of its components.

history.text: The Shuowen preserves the “stop the weapons” explanation attributed to King Zhuang of Chu. Wiktionary instead takes 止 here as a foot or walking element and interprets the combination as a military expedition. The difference turns on which sense of 止 is assigned to the component.

uncertainties.text: The expedition account is Wiktionary’s interpretation; the cited passage does not present the early inscriptions needed to assess it directly. The traditional peace-through-disarmament reading can be discussed as an influential interpretation without presenting it as a proven account of the character’s creation.
